docs.text:
to_config(
    *, seed: int, fixed_atoms: bool = False
) -> IntegratorConfig

The IntegratorConfig of this record with seed (the Simulation's); fixed_atoms: whether the structure has FixAtoms (fixcm="auto").

docs.title: LangevinBAOAB dataclass
docs.text:
Langevin-Hoover NPT, ASE 3.27's LangevinBAOAB on the graph engine (SPEC §10.2).

  • friction_per_fs: the thermostat friction; ASE's T_tau is 1 / friction, as in main.py (workflow.baoab_settings);
  • pressure_GPa or external_stress_GPa (ASE's externalstress sign: a scalar or six Voigt components), not both;
  • cell_mode: "hydrostatic" (ASE hydrostatic=True) or "full";
  • barostat_tau_fs: ASE's P_tau, None = ASE's default 20 T_tau;
  • barostat_mass_factor: ASE's P_mass_factor;
  • disable_cell_langevin: as ASE;
  • max_volume_ratio and max_cell_length_A: the cell-divergence stop (3b-T07). A Simulation stops with CellDivergedError (restart and metadata written first) once the volume leaves [V0 / ratio, V0 ratio], V0 the run's starting volume, or a cell vector is longer than max_cell_length_A (1000 Å: float32 coordinates still resolve 6e-5 Å there). A vapour at a low pressure expands without bound otherwise, until the coordinates lose their precision. None turns a limit off.

The production drag term is the corrected one (SPEC §12.1, 1b-T09); ASE's own variant stays an IntegratorConfig option for comparisons with ASE.

docs.title: moves
docs.text:
MC move records and their attempts (SPEC §10.4; contracts: plan task 3-T01).

Swap, Transmute and Displace are frozen records a user builds before any model is loaded, so this module imports neither torch nor MACE nor ASE. They are checked against the workload and the superset by Simulation.run(mc=...) (§7.6). Species stay as given (symbols or atomic numbers); the driver maps them to atomic numbers. build_attempt builds the captured attempt of a move: 3-T09 (swaps, transmutations), 3-T10 (displacements, fastmace.mc.displace).

docs.title: Swap dataclass
docs.text: Swap the species of two atoms (§10.4): a pair type uniformly from pairs, then one atom of each species uniformly. every MD steps, then attempts attempts. velocities: exchange (default; the atoms swap velocities), rescale, redraw or redraw_all.

docs.title: Transmute dataclass
docs.text:
Change one atom's species within the transmutable set species (§10.4, semi-grand canonical).

velocities: rescale, redraw or redraw_all; None takes the default (rescale, or redraw_all when the integrator fixes the centre of mass). mu: configurational chemical potential differences in eV against a reference species (configurational_mu converts full ones); absent species have 0. formal_charges: q_s per species (0 if absent), for the parity rule ΔZ − Δq even (§10.4 "Charge and spin"). Both are stored as sorted pairs.

docs.title: Displace dataclass
docs.text: Displace one atom uniformly within a sphere of radius delta_A (§10.4). adaptive=True tunes δ during equilibration only, and the value is recorded.

docs.title: configurational_mu
docs.text:
configurational_mu(
    mu_full: Mapping[Any, float],
    temperature_K: float,
    reference: Any,
    masses: Mapping[Any, float] | None = None,
) -> dict[Any, float]

Configurational chemical-potential differences from full ones (§10.4): Δμ_s^conf = Δμ_s^full + (3/2) k_B T ln(m_s / m_ref).

mu_full maps species to Δμ_s^full in eV relative to reference (whose own entry, if given, must be 0). masses in amu, by species; None takes ASE's standard atomic masses. The result has the keys of mu_full, for fm.mc.Transmute(mu=...).

fm.load (SPEC §7.1): the checkpoint as a pristine model, e3nn in float64 on the CPU.

source is a label ("mh1-r2scan"), an alias with head= ("mh1"), a path or a URL. A multi-head checkpoint needs head= or a label that names one; otherwise ValueError lists its heads. A path or URL is unpickled only with a matching sha256= or trusted=True; a label's file must match the table (SPEC §7.6). download=True fetches a missing file into the models cache and checks it before it is kept. The trust decision and the hash are in provenance(). The plan converts the model to its backend and precision; the pristine model itself is never changed (fm.ForceField). Before MACE is imported, the OEq runtime is prepared where the hybrid is possible (prepare_hybrid_if_possible; the outcome is oeq_runtime). The expandable-segments allocator is configured first (configure_allocator, a no-op if PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF is set): preparing the hybrid can touch CUDA, and the allocator reads the variable only once (5-T07).

docs.title: ForceField
docs.text:
ForceField(model, atoms=None, *, precision="float32", rewrites="auto", species=None).

  • model: an fm.load result (a LoadedModel, normally the pristine e3nn float64 CPU model) or a label, which is loaded with fm.load. A path needs fm.load first, because the trust decision needs one (§7.6);
  • atoms: optional; its species are the default superset (§7.1 passes it). Without it the superset is the species of the first structure the force field is used with;
  • precision: the force precision, "float32" or "float64" (§7.3);
  • rewrites: "auto" or a RewriteConfig; resolved per plan;
  • species: the declared superset (§8.5), symbols or atomic numbers, compared as a set; a species without an embedding raises ModelElementError. It may be larger than the structure's species (phase 3, rule 8): every species-indexed table is built for it, so an atom can become any superset species in place (3-T02);
  • dispersion: None, "d3bj" or an fm.D3 (SPEC §7.7, §11.2). "d3bj" expands from the model's training functional (fastmace.longrange.d3.expand: ValueError when it is unknown or already contains dispersion); an explicit record whose functional differs from the training one is kept with a warning in dispersion_warnings. The complete record is dispersion and part of the identity. Refused (PlanRefused): the ATM term (d3-three-body) and PolarMACE (d3-polar, decision 41). Plans carry the record and put the D3 term into their force field (fastmace.model.dispersed, 3b-T04).

What the run will do (SPEC §9.2). Only max_temperature_K is required.

  • max_temperature_K: the highest thermostat target of the run, K; sizes the skin and the bucket headroom (rule 11). Simulation.run refuses a schedule above it (§7.6);
  • species_changes: swaps, transmutations or species events (§8.5);
  • atom_count_changes: reserved; the planner refuses it in 1.0 (§9.3 rule 7, §8.6);
  • min_mc_temperature_K: the lowest MC target temperature, K; the ΔE gate threshold 0.01 k_B T_min (§12.3). Required when mc_moves is non-empty, and positive;
  • host_callbacks_every: user Python every n steps (rule 9); None = no callbacks;
  • needs_per_atom: per-atom outputs the run needs ("energies", "charges", ...);
  • mc_moves: declared move types ("swap", "transmute", "displace");
  • reproducible: bitwise within the scope of §9.3; the planner refuses what it cannot guarantee (in 1b: everything, "no family qualified");
  • mc_energy_precision: §10.4; "auto" = the force precision if the ΔE gate passes;
  • max_displacement_A: the largest displacement δ, Å, any Displace move of the run may use (adaptive δ included). Required when "displace" is in mc_moves; rule 11 adds 2δ to the skin (§10.4), and attaching a Displace with a larger delta_A is refused.

GPU structure relaxations, fixed and variable cell (SPEC §10.3).

This package's namespace is fm.optimize: the public optimiser records (plan task 4-T01, conductor's choice 1), which a Simulation takes as optimizer= (4-T05) and which map onto OptimizerConfig. The implementations (lbfgs.py, 4-T05; fire.py, 4-T06; cell.py, 4-T07) are built by the planner only, over a base.DOFView (SPEC §5); importing this package imports neither them nor torch.

The optimisers take ASE 3.27's arguments and defaults; lengths are Angstrom. FIRE's dt and dtmax are in ASE time units, as ASE's (they are step-size parameters, not physical times). FrechetCell is ASE's FrechetCellFilter with the pressure in GPa.

docs.title: output
docs.text:
Output: where a Simulation writes and how often, and the chunked writer (SPEC §7.2, §10.6).

Output is the record (plan task 1b-T01). ChunkedOutput (plan task 1b-T06) writes the thermo rows and trajectory frames of a run as chunks, thermo.<n>.csv and trajectory.<n>.traj for n = 0, 1, ..., with a chunk boundary exactly at every restart point (SPEC §10.6 "Output files at restart points"):

  • restart_point() closes the current chunks, fsyncs them and their directory (plan task 2-T10; rows and frames in between are flushed, not fsynced) and opens the next pair; it returns the indices the restart file stores (io.restart.OUTPUT_KEYS): output_chunk, the last closed chunk, and output_rows and output_frames, the rows and frames in chunks 0 to output_chunk. Call it after draining the output queue (AsyncOutput.restart_point does both), then write the restart file. Every restart write is a chunk boundary, a stop request's included.
  • Resume (resume_from= those indices) checks the chunks up to output_chunk (present, with the stored numbers of rows and frames) and that every later chunk can be deleted, before it touches anything; otherwise it raises RestartMismatch. Then it deletes the later chunks and opens chunk output_chunk + 1. Nothing is ever rewritten: the research engine's resume reread and rewrote md.traj (workflow.truncate_outputs, up to 770 MB on the NAS).

Rows and frames written after the last restart point (by the asynchronous writer, or before a crash) are thus in later chunks only. A crash between restart_point and the restart write leaves the older restart file, and resume from it deletes the newer chunks as well.

Every chunk is complete on its own: each thermo chunk starts with the header, and a chunk without rows or frames still has both files (an empty trajectory reads as no frames). read_thermo and read_frames concatenate the chunks in order; ase.io.read(path, index=":") reads one. This module imports neither torch nor ASE at import time (fm.Output is a light name).

docs.title: schedule
docs.text:
Temperature schedules: ramps and holds, whole steps, the target per step (SPEC §7.2, §7.6 "Schedules").

A Schedule is timestep-free: segments in ps. Schedule.resolve(timestep_fs) rounds each segment to whole steps (half up) and records the boundaries, the total and the rounded durations and rates. The target is piecewise linear in the step. Step n of a segment uses the target at the step's end point, as the research engine does ("update the target every timestep using that step's endpoint", docs/protocol.md), so the target changes every step on a ramp and never on a hold. It reaches the integrator through Integrator.set_temperature before the step (TargetFill), never as an event.

Each ramp interpolates from its colder end, T_low + (T_high - T_low) * w. This reproduces the research engine's float expressions bit for bit: peak * n / H when heating from 0 K and final + (peak - final) * (H + C - n) / C when cooling.

ScheduleState is the schedule position: the restart record of SimulationState.protocol.

Run MD on structure (path or Atoms) with model and return a RunResult.

Arguments as SPEC §7.7 level 2:

  • model: a label, path or URL, with head, charge, spin_multiplicity and sha256/trusted as fm.load; or an fm.load result (then without those);
  • ensemble: "NVT" (Langevin), "NPT" (BAOAB with pressure_GPa and cell_mode) or "NVE" (velocity Verlet from the structure's momenta, no temperature_K). integrator= chooses any fm.integrators record explicitly;
  • temperature_K or schedule (an fm.protocols schedule); steps (optional with a schedule: the whole schedule);
  • mc and min_mc_temperature_K: one fm.mc record or a sequence of them, checked as §7.7 says, attached where the target is at or above min_mc_temperature_K;
  • dispersion: None, "d3bj" or an fm.D3: the complete record goes into the force field (MACE plus D3, SPEC §11.2) and is shown in the report; a functional other than the training one is a report warning;
  • repeat: the supercell, (1, 1, 1) by default (never expanded silently);
  • output: a directory or an fm.Output; default ./<structure stem>.fastmace/, or ./fastmace-run/ for an Atoms;
  • seed: the noise seed; None draws one, recorded in metadata.json;
  • check: as Simulation (the gate is opt-in, check="gate");
  • mode, allow_reference, fallback, gate, runner, engine, neighbours: the planner inputs, passed to Simulation as they are (simulation.PlannerOptions);
  • calibrate: True measures the backends the rules rank equal (hybrid against plain cuEq) on this structure before the run and takes plain cuEq only if it is faster by more than 5 % in every pair (SPEC §9.1, decision 55; CalibrationConfig, planner.calibrate). Off by default: it costs four child builds. Refused with MC moves.

Every ValueError and refusal comes before the model is loaded.

  • summary: the one-screen report (§7.7, 1b-T15), simulation.report.text() after the run;
  • plan, gate: the Plan and gate records (§9.5, §12.3);
  • simulation: the Simulation, for restarts and the expert API; its output is flushed and it can run on (simulation.run);
  • metadata: the dict written to metadata.json (§13);

docs.title: Simulation
docs.text:
MD on the graph engine with a plan, an optional gate, schedules and complete restarts.

Simulation(atoms, force_field, *, species=None, integrator, workload=None, output=None, seed, check="skip", allow_naive_cueq=False, mode=None, allow_reference=False, fallback=None, gate=None, runner=None, engine=None, neighbours=None, adaptation=None, calibration=None):

  • atoms: ASE Atoms, full 3D PBC (§4.4); copied, the caller's object is never changed;
  • force_field: a fm.ForceField, an fm.load result or a label; a model is wrapped in a float32 ForceField with species= (default: the structure's species). A path raises TypeError (load it with fm.load, the trust decision needs one); species with a ForceField raises ValueError (the ForceField owns the superset);
  • integrator: an fm.integrators record (fm.integrators.RECORDS); a scheme not registered yet is refused by the plan (rule 1);
  • workload: fm.Workload; default Workload(max_temperature_K=integrator.temperature_K);
  • output: fm.Output; thermo rows, trajectory frames and metadata.json go to its directory, in chunks (§10.6). None writes no file;
  • seed: the integrator's noise seed, recorded;
  • check: one of CHECK_MODES;
  • allow_naive_cueq: accept cuEquivariance's naive kernels (§9.2), recorded;
  • the planner inputs (PlannerOptions, recorded in simulation.json): mode (§9.3; None lets the planner choose), allow_reference (rule 1), fallback (FallbackConfig, §9.4), gate (GateConfig, §12.3 "Resources"; the record is sim.gate_config, the result sim.gate), runner (RunnerConfig, §8.7), engine (EngineConfig) and neighbours (NeighbourConfig), adaptation (AdaptationConfig, §9.6) and calibration (CalibrationConfig, §9.1; both phase 5, plan task 5-T01). docs.title: relax
docs.text:
relax(
    *, fmax: float = 0.05, steps: int = 100000000
) -> tuple[Any, dict[str, Any]]

Relax with the optimiser (SPEC §10.3; 4-T05): ASE's Optimizer.run(fmax=, steps=) on the engine.

A converged start takes no step; otherwise one step at a time until the largest constraint-adjusted force is below fmax (eV/Angstrom) or steps steps are done, one force call per step. A second call continues with the optimiser's history, as a second run of one ASE optimiser does. Returns the relaxed Atoms (a copy of the structure at the committed positions and cell, no calculator) and the summary of fastmace.optimize.driver.relax: steps, converged, seconds, initial and final energies per atom, fmax, the per-step energies and max forces, and the engine's neighbour rebuilds and re-captures.

docs.title: save_restart
docs.text:
save_restart(path: Any) -> None

Write the complete §10.6 state at the current committed step, a canonical restart point.

path is <directory>/restart.npz (or the directory): Simulation.resume(directory) reads it there. The output queue is drained and the output chunks end here (§10.6), the engine is canonicalised and written by io.restart.write_engine_restart (T05's format), and simulation.json next to it holds what that format does not: the model source, the integrator record, workload, Output, seed, allow_naive_cueq, the planner options, species, masses and PBC. A plan that runs in a child copies the child's last hand-off, a canonical restart point at the committed step (2-T07).

Only at a committed step: refused (RuntimeError) inside an MC block and while the engine holds an uncommitted (overflowed) step, before anything is written (§10.6, 3-T08).

docs.text:
resume(
    directory: Any,
    *,
    allow_plan_change: bool = False,
    check: Check = "skip",
) -> Simulation

Continue from the restart in directory. A different force-field identity raises RestartMismatch, except that another MACE or FastMACE version alone warns and is recorded as a plan revision and in the report (owner decision 23); a different plan needs allow_plan_change=True and makes a new revision (§9.5, §10.6). check as in the constructor.

The model is loaded again from simulation.json's file, checked against its SHA-256; the engine is built at the restart's positions, cell and composition (species and masses at the restart step, not the initial structure's; 3-T08) through the planner, then takes the restart's state, edge bucket and neighbour capacity (io.restart.resume_engine). Output chunks after the restart point are deleted and new ones opened; nothing is rewritten.

docs.title: set_positions
docs.text:
set_positions(positions: Any) -> None

Host write of positions at a canonical point: quiesce, write, rebuild, re-evaluate (owner decision D4). positions in Å, shape (N, 3); the momenta stay.

docs.title: set_momenta
docs.text:
set_momenta(momenta: Any) -> None

Host write of momenta at a canonical point (owner decision D4). momenta in ASE units, shape (N, 3); the engine integrates velocities, momenta / masses.

docs.title: update
docs.text:
update(
    *,
    species: Any = None,
    masses: Any = None,
    charges: Any = None,
    total_charge: Any = None,
    friction_per_fs: Any = None,
    positions: Any = None,
    momenta: Any = None,
    cell: Any = None,
) -> None

Any combination of host changes as one transaction with one force evaluation (SPEC §8.5, §7.7).

  • species: atomic numbers or symbols, (N,); in the ForceField's superset (SpeciesNotInSuperset). Masses follow the new species' standard masses unless masses is given too;
  • masses: amu, (N,); the momenta stay (ASE), so the velocities change;
  • charges: per-atom charges, (N,), and total_charge, for models that take them;
  • friction_per_fs: the Langevin friction in 1/fs (the record's unit); it drops the captured graphs, which bake it in (a recorded re-capture), and with the default barostat τ moves P_tau and the barostat mass with it;
  • positions (Å) and momenta (ASE units), (N, 3); momenta use the new masses;
  • cell (Å, (3, 3), rows the lattice vectors), fixed-cell runs only (4-T05; 4-T09 relaxes quench frames with their own NPT cells on one engine): the positions are not scaled, so give them too. The lists and cell inputs change in place, so the captured graphs stay unless the rebuild grows a capacity or the edge count needs a new padded size.

Everything is validated before anything is written. The changes apply in this order: species, masses, charges, friction, cell, positions, momenta; then a canonical point (neighbour list rebuilt at the committed positions, forces and stress evaluated once, integrator.start), as a host write of positions (owner decision D4). Nothing given: nothing happens.

docs.title: set_species
docs.text:
set_species(species: Any) -> None

Set every atom's species (atomic numbers or symbols, shape (N,)), one event. Each must be in the ForceField's superset (SpeciesNotInSuperset); masses follow the new species' standard masses unless set_masses follows.

docs.title: set_masses
docs.text:
set_masses(masses: Any) -> None

Set every atom's mass in amu, shape (N,), one event; the momenta stay (ASE), so the velocities change: v' = v m_old / m_new.

docs.title: set_charges
docs.text:
set_charges(
    charges: Any, *, total_charge: float | None = None
) -> None

Set the per-atom charges (models that take them), shape (N,), and optionally the total charge, one event. charges=None with total_charge changes the total only.

docs.title: set_friction
docs.text:
set_friction(friction_per_fs: float) -> None

Set the Langevin friction in 1/fs, one event; it drops the graphs that bake c1/c2 in (a recorded re-capture).

docs.title: Committed dataclass
docs.text:
The committed step as read-only host arrays: what an observer sees (Simulation.committed).

stress (3×3, eV/Å³) is None for fixed-cell integrators; energy in eV. The composition (3-T03): species atomic numbers (N,), masses amu (N,), charges (N,) or None for models that take none.

docs.title: Port your ASE script
docs.text:
FastMACE offers three ways in from ASE. They all use the same force field, planner, gate and restart files.

You have Use Speed a tool that needs only a calculator (phonopy, NEB, your own optimiser) fm.calc compiled tier, no CUDA graphs an ASE MD or optimiser script fastmace.ase classes full graph-engine speed a new run fm.md or fm.Simulation full graph-engine speed

docs.title: Level 0: a calculator, fm.calc
docs.text:
import fastmace as fm

atoms.calc = fm.calc("mh1", head="matpes_r2scan")
energy = atoms.get_potential_energy()
forces = atoms.get_forces()
stress = atoms.get_stress()

fm.calc wraps fastmace.ase.FastMACECalculator. ASE calls a calculator once per step from Python, so a calculator cannot use CUDA graphs over the whole step. You get the compiled model and the exact rewrites, not the full speed-up. FastMACE prints this once: use fm.md or the fastmace.ase integrators for full speed.

docs.title: Level 1: change the import
docs.text:
An ASE Langevin script:

from ase import units
from ase.md.langevin import Langevin

atoms.calc = mace_mp(...)
dyn = Langevin(atoms, 0.5 * units.fs, temperature_K=300, friction=0.02 / units.fs,
               trajectory="run.traj", logfile="run.log", loginterval=20)
dyn.attach(print_energy, interval=1000)
dyn.run(1_000_000)

becomes:

from ase import units
from fastmace.ase import Langevin

dyn = Langevin(atoms, 0.5 * units.fs, temperature_K=300, friction=0.02 / units.fs,
               model="mh1", head="matpes_r2scan", trajectory="run.traj",
               logfile="run.log", loginterval=20)
dyn.attach(print_energy, interval=1000)
dyn.run(1_000_000)
print(dyn.summary)        # the run report

Rules:

  • Arguments keep ASE 3.27's names and units. friction is in ASE's inverse time units, as in ASE. The shim never reinterprets an ASE argument. An argument that is neither supported nor explicitly refused raises TypeError naming it.
  • Refused: rng (pass seed=; the noise comes from FastMACE's device generator), a non-default communicator, and master.
  • FastMACE additions are keyword-only: model= or force_field=, head=, seed=, output=, check=, dispersion=.
  • Files: trajectory= and logfile= keep their ASE meaning and format, so your analysis scripts work unchanged. Everything else (metadata.json, the report, restart files) goes to output=, by default <trajectory stem>.fastmace/.
  • Observers see the committed state in atoms, and get_potential_energy(), get_forces() and get_stress() return the engine's values without a new evaluation. An observer may change positions, momenta, species, masses or charges; FastMACE applies the change as one event. Changing the atom count, PBC, cell, constraints or atoms.calc raises, because each would invalidate the plan.
  • FastMACE members: summary, plan, gate, metadata, simulation (the underlying fm.Simulation) and output.

docs.title: Mapped classes
docs.text:
ASE 3.27 class fastmace.ase class FastMACE integrator Langevin Langevin fm.integrators.Langevin LangevinBAOAB LangevinBAOAB fm.integrators.LangevinBAOAB VelocityVerlet VelocityVerlet fm.integrators.NVE Bussi Bussi fm.integrators.CSVR NoseHooverChainNVT NoseHooverChainNVT fm.integrators.NoseHooverChain IsotropicMTKNPT, MTKNPT same names fm.integrators.MTK NVTBerendsen, NPTBerendsen, Inhomogeneous_NPTBerendsen same names fm.integrators.Berendsen LBFGS, FIRE (optimisers) LBFGS, FIRE fm.optimize.LBFGS, fm.optimize.FIRE

An ASE class without a mapping raises PlanRefused with the list of mapped ones. The shim never falls back to ASE's own loop silently.

docs.title: Resume a shim run
docs.text:
import fastmace as fm

sim = fm.Simulation.resume("run.fastmace/")
sim.run()

The resumed run continues in FastMACE's chunked output format in that directory (see Output, restart and resume).

docs.title: Level 2: one call, fm.md
docs.text:
import fastmace as fm

run = fm.md("NaCl.cif", model="mh1", head="matpes_r2scan", ensemble="NVT",
            temperature_K=300, steps=1_000_000, repeat=(3, 3, 3),
            output="run/", seed=1)
print(run.summary)

See FastMACE in five minutes for the arguments and the command-line equivalent, fastmace md.

docs.title: Monte Carlo and swaps
docs.text:
Experimental

MC moves carry an "experimental: not yet qualified" line in the run report until their qualification study is recorded.

FastMACE runs hybrid MD/MC: MD steps on the graph engine, with blocks of MC attempts in between. Species changes are transactional events inside the captured graph, so a swap does not cost a re-capture. The species superset (every species the run may contain) is declared up front.

docs.title: Move records
docs.text:
Record Move fm.mc.Swap(pairs=[("O", "Cl")], every=100, attempts=50) swap the species of two atoms; velocities="exchange" (default), "rescale", "redraw" or "redraw_all" fm.mc.Transmute(species=("Na", "K"), every=..., attempts=..., mu={...}) semi-grand canonical species change; mu are configurational chemical-potential differences in eV, fm.mc.configurational_mu converts full ones fm.mc.Displace(delta_A=0.1, every=..., attempts=...) displace one atom in a sphere; adaptive=True tunes δ during equilibration

Each attempt is accepted by the Metropolis rule at the thermostat's current target temperature. The thermo output has mc_<move>_attempted and mc_<move>_accepted columns, and the counters survive restarts.

docs.title: With fm.md
docs.text:
import fastmace as fm

run = fm.md("NaNbOCl4.cif", model="mh1", head="matpes_r2scan",
            temperature_K=600, steps=200_000,
            mc=fm.mc.Swap(pairs=[("O", "Cl")], every=100, attempts=50),
            output="swap/", seed=1)

fm.md infers the species superset and the workload from mc=. With a constant temperature the MC temperature is that temperature, which must be positive. With a schedule, min_mc_temperature_K= is required: MC blocks attach only where the schedule's target is at or above it.

docs.title: With Simulation
docs.text:
model = fm.load("mh1", head="matpes_r2scan")
ff = fm.ForceField(model, atoms, species=["Na", "Nb", "Cl", "O"])
sim = fm.Simulation(
    atoms, ff,
    integrator=fm.integrators.Langevin(timestep_fs=1.0, temperature_K=600, friction_per_fs=0.002),
    workload=fm.Workload(max_temperature_K=1000, species_changes=True, mc_moves=("swap",),
                         min_mc_temperature_K=250),
    output=fm.Output("run/"), seed=1,
)
sim.run(steps=100_000)                                    # MD only
sim.run(steps=100_000, mc=fm.mc.Swap(pairs=[("O", "Cl")], every=100, attempts=50))
sim.run(steps=50_000)                                     # the swap block stays attached
sim.run(steps=50_000, mc=None)                            # detach

A move set stays attached until a later run passes another mc= or mc=None. A species outside the superset raises SpeciesNotInSuperset.

docs.title: From TOML
docs.text:
[[mc]]
move = "swap"
pairs = [["O", "Cl"]]
every = 100
attempts = 50

docs.title: Charge and spin
docs.text: For models that read charges (PolarMACE) or a total charge or spin (OMOL-0), a transmutation must keep ΔZ − Δq even (formal_charges=), or it is refused with ChargeParityRefused.

docs.title: Labels
docs.text:
fm.load, fm.md, fm.calc and the CLI take a model as a label, a local path or a URL. List the labels with:

fastmace models
Label Head Licence Kind mp0-medium, mp0-large, mp0b3-medium, mpa0-medium MIT MACE-MP foundation models (PBE) omat0-medium, matpes-pbe, matpes-r2scan ASL OMAT and MatPES models mh1-omat, mh1-mp, mh1-r2scan fixed by the label ASL MACE-MH-1 with one head mh1 head= required ASL MACE-MH-1, any of its six heads polar1-s, polar1-m, polar1-l ASL MACE-POLAR-1 (needs [polar]) omol0-xl (omol0) omol ASL MACE-OMOL-0, molecules; takes charge= and spin_multiplicity= off23-small, off23-medium, off23-large, off23b-medium, off24-medium ASL MACE-OFF, organic molecules and crystals

fastmace models prints the file names and SHA-256 of each checkpoint.

docs.title: Heads
docs.text: A multi-head checkpoint without head= raises ValueError listing its heads. There is no default head. MH-1's heads are matpes_r2scan, mp_pbe_refit_add, spice_wB97M, oc20_usemppbe, omol and omat_pbe.

docs.title: Where checkpoints come from
docs.text:
fm.load(label) looks for the file in $FASTMACE_MODELS, then in <cache root>/models. With download=True it fetches the file from its official URL and checks the SHA-256 before keeping it. FastMACE never ships or redistributes model weights.

A file outside the label table needs sha256= (its expected hash) or trusted=True, because loading a checkpoint runs pickled code.

docs.title: Licences
docs.text:
The weights' licence binds you independently of FastMACE's MIT licence. Several foundation models, MACE-MH-1 among them, are under the Academic Software License (ASL, non-commercial use only). FastMACE shows each model's licence once per process as a ModelLicenceWarning, and the run report has a licence: line read from the label table.

FastMACE's own licence and its dependencies' licences are on the Licences page.

docs.title: Which model for what
docs.text:
• Inorganic crystals: MH-1 (mh1-r2scan or mh1 with a head), OMAT-0 or MP-0. MH-1 runs at its fastest in FastMACE through the MH-1 rewrites.
  • Long-range electrostatics: MACE-POLAR-1. POLAR-1-S showed a Fukui charge runaway on NaNbO3, and all POLAR sizes failed on NaTaO3 in our tests.
  • Molecules: OMOL-0 (charge and spin) or MACE-OFF (organic elements only: H, C, N, O, F, P, S, Cl, Br, I).
  • Dispersion: see NPT and D3. MACE-OFF, OMOL-0 and MH-1's omol head already contain dispersion, so dispersion="d3bj" is refused for them.

docs.title: NPT and D3 dispersion
docs.text:
Experimental

NPT and D3 carry an "experimental: not yet qualified" line in the run report until their qualification studies are recorded.

docs.title: NPT
docs.text:
ensemble="NPT" in fm.md (and --ensemble NPT on the command line) is ASE 3.27's LangevinBAOAB barostat on the graph engine:

run = fm.md("NbCl5.cif", model="mh1", head="matpes_r2scan", ensemble="NPT",
            temperature_K=300, pressure_GPa=0.0, cell_mode="hydrostatic",
            steps=200_000, repeat=(3, 3, 3), dispersion="d3bj", output="npt/", seed=1)

cell_mode is "hydrostatic" or "full". For other barostats, pass an explicit integrator:

Record ASE class fm.integrators.LangevinBAOAB(...) LangevinBAOAB fm.integrators.MTK(..., cell_mode="hydrostatic" or "full") IsotropicMTKNPT, MTKNPT fm.integrators.Berendsen(..., pressure_GPa=...) NPTBerendsen, Inhomogeneous_NPTBerendsen (equilibration only, non-canonical)

Cell divergence. A vapour at low pressure expands without bound. LangevinBAOAB stops the run with CellDivergedError (restart and metadata written first) once the volume leaves [V0/20, 20 V0] or a cell vector is longer than 1000 Å. Change the limits with max_volume_ratio and max_cell_length_A.

Stress convention. The force field returns the potential (virial) stress as a full 3x3 tensor in ASE's sign convention; the integrator adds the kinetic part, as ASE's get_stress(include_ideal_gas=True) does.

docs.title: D3(BJ) dispersion
docs.text:
FastMACE has its own GPU D3(BJ) term. It runs inside the captured step in MD, in relaxations and in quenches, and needs no extra package.

run = fm.md(..., dispersion="d3bj")

"d3bj" is shorthand. FastMACE expands it to a complete fm.D3 record before planning: Becke-Johnson damping with the parameter set of the head's training functional (pbe for PBE-trained models, r2scan for matpes_r2scan), 40 bohr pair and coordination cutoffs, no three-body term, float64. The expanded record is printed in the report and recorded in metadata.json.

"d3bj" is refused when:

  • the training reference already contains dispersion (MACE-OFF, OMOL-0, MH-1's omol head), since D3 would count it twice;
  • the training functional is unknown (POLAR-1, or a model loaded from a path or URL). Pass an explicit record then:
run = fm.md(..., model="polar1-m", dispersion=fm.D3(functional="pbe"))

An explicit fm.D3 is used as given; a functional that differs from the training functional is a report warning. In TOML, a [dispersion] table holds the record's fields.

When to use it. The molecular chlorides need D3 in NPT: without it, NbCl5 swelled by 20 % at 300 K and evaporated at 600 K in our tests.

docs.title: The planner
docs.text:
Every Simulation (and so every fm.md, fastmace md and fastmace.ase run) starts with a plan. The planner reads the model, the structure, the integrator, the workload, the installed software and the GPU, and decides:

  • the tier: the CUDA-graph engine (fastest), the compiled tier without graphs, the eager hybrid, or the reference path;
  • the backend: the cuEquivariance/OpenEquivariance hybrid, or plain cuEquivariance;
  • the precision of the force evaluation (float32 by default; integration is always float64);
  • which rewrites are on, and the reason for each one that is off;
  • the neighbour-list skin and buffer sizes.

Rules are general: there are no per-GPU or per-crystal tuning tables. Every rewrite is exact to rounding and is checked against the original MACE module when it is applied.

docs.title: Read the plan
docs.text:
model = fm.load("mh1", head="matpes_r2scan")
sim = fm.Simulation(atoms, model, integrator=..., seed=1)
print(sim.plan)                  # str(plan): about 30 lines, by section
print(sim.plan.describe(full=True))   # every decision with its rule and reason

str(plan) gives a short overview: the tier, backend and precision, the hard rules that decided them, the rewrites that are on and the ones that are off with a short reason. describe(full=True) lists every decision. The same text is in the run report and in metadata.json.

plan.decision(key) returns (item, choice, reason) for one decision, and plan.overrides() lists the options you set explicitly.

docs.title: Influence the plan
docs.text:
• Workload: fm.Workload(max_temperature_K=..., species_changes=..., mc_moves=..., host_callbacks_every=...) tells the planner what the run will do. fm.md infers it from its arguments. A schedule above max_temperature_K is refused, because the skin was sized for it.
  • Mode: Simulation(mode=...) asks for a tier; None lets the planner choose.
  • Rewrites and precision live on the force field: fm.ForceField(model, atoms, precision="float32", rewrites="auto").
  • An option the planner cannot honour raises PlanRefused with every reason, before the first step. Nothing is substituted silently.

docs.title: The gate
docs.text: check="gate" evaluates the planned engine on your structure (and rattled copies) against a float64 reference before the first step. If it fails, the fallback searches for the closest plan that passes, turning off rewrites one by one, and records what it did. The gate is opt-in; the default is check="skip". The record is sim.gate.

docs.title: Runtime adaptation
docs.text: During a run the planner watches re-captures and buffer overflows. Past a budget it may switch tier at a committed step, or fall back after a capture error, and the report's runtime line records it. A resume rebuilds the recorded revision exactly.

docs.title: When the run did not get the graph engine
docs.text:
The report says why and what would change it: a structure that is not 3D periodic, a missing OpenEquivariance (fastmace doctor names the piece), a model outside the rewrite registry, padded edges that are not exactly zero, a failed self-check, or a fallback after a failed gate.

For the full rule list see SPEC section 9 and the planner design note.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
fastmace relax NaCl.cif --model mh1 --head matpes_r2scan --optimizer gpu-LBFGS --fmax 0.01
fastmace relax NaCl.cif --model mh1 --head matpes_r2scan --optimizer gpu-FIRE --cell-filter frechet --pressure 0
fastmace quench run/ --into gpu --optimizer gpu-LBFGS
Optimizer name Runs on gpu-LBFGS (default) the graph engine gpu-FIRE the graph engine ase-LBFGS, ase-BFGS ASE's optimisers on fm.calc LBFGS, BFGS ASE's (so existing protocol files keep their meaning)

gpu-LBFGS reproduces the annealing-benchmark minima of ASE's LBFGS.

fastmace relax writes the relaxed structure (--output, default <stem>.relaxed.extxyz) with a .json summary and a .log.

fastmace quench RUN_DIR quenches frames of a finished run, chosen as a protocol's quench picks them. Each frame keeps its own cell. --into NAME writes RUN_DIR/quench-NAME/, so one run can be quenched with several optimisers side by side. A GPU quench relaxes all its frames on one engine.

docs.title: Python: Simulation.relax
docs.text:
import fastmace as fm

model = fm.load("mh1", head="matpes_r2scan")
opt = fm.optimize.LBFGS()                                  # ASE 3.27's defaults
opt = fm.optimize.FIRE(cell_filter=fm.optimize.FrechetCell(scalar_pressure_GPa=0.0))
sim = fm.Simulation(atoms, model, optimizer=opt, seed=0)
relaxed, summary = sim.relax(fmax=0.01)

A relaxation Simulation takes optimizer= instead of integrator= and writes no output files (pass no output=).

docs.title: Python: ASE-style optimisers
docs.text:
from ase.filters import FrechetCellFilter
from fastmace.ase import LBFGS

opt = LBFGS(FrechetCellFilter(atoms), model="mh1", head="matpes_r2scan")
opt.run(fmax=0.01)

fastmace.ase.LBFGS and FIRE take ASE 3.27's arguments. use_line_search=True, position_reset_callback and the deprecated maxmove are refused. They take Atoms or FrechetCellFilter; other cell filters are refused with the reason.

docs.title: Anneal and quench protocols
docs.text:
schedule="anneal" (or the profiles slow, fast, ultrafast) runs a temperature schedule; fm.protocols.ramp and fm.protocols.hold build your own:

anneal = fm.protocols.ramp(0, 1000, ps=20) + fm.protocols.ramp(1000, 250, rate_K_per_ps=-3)
sim.run(schedule=anneal)

A protocol file's [relax] and [quench] tables take the same optimizer names.

docs.title: What a run writes
docs.text:
fm.Output("run/", trajectory_every=20, thermo_every=20, restart_every=10_000) (the fm.md defaults) writes into run/:

File Content thermo.<n>.csv thermo rows (step, time, temperature, energies, pressure for NPT), each chunk with its header trajectory.<n>.traj ASE trajectory frames restart.npz the complete simulation state at the last restart point simulation.json the inputs and planner options, for resume metadata.json plan, gate, report, provenance (versions, model hash, GPU)

The outputs are written in chunks, n = 0, 1, ..., with a chunk boundary at every restart point. Each chunk is complete on its own: ase.io.read("run/trajectory.0.traj", index=":") reads one. To read a whole run in order:

from fastmace.io.output import read_frames, read_thermo

frames = read_frames("run/")
thermo = read_thermo("run/")

Output is asynchronous: a snapshot is copied to the host and written while the next step runs, so writing does not slow the GPU.

docs.title: Restart
docs.text:
A restart file holds the complete state: positions, momenta, cell, barostat and thermostat state, the RNG state, species after MC exchanges, the schedule position, the MC counters and the plan revision. Restart points are written every restart_every steps and on a clean stop.

sim.save_restart("run/restart.npz")         # an extra one by hand
sim = fm.Simulation.resume("run/")          # continue
sim.run()                                   # the rest of the schedule

Resume checks the chunks up to the restart point, deletes later chunks (rows and frames written after the restart point) and continues with the next chunk. Nothing is rewritten. If the stored chunks do not match, it raises RestartMismatch before touching anything.

A resume rebuilds the recorded plan. If the software or GPU changed so that the plan would differ, it refuses unless you pass allow_plan_change=True. A resume never falls back.

docs.title: Reproducibility
docs.text: Hybrid runs (the default backend) use atomic sums and are not bitwise reproducible; compare them statistically. A resumed run agrees bit for bit with an uninterrupted one in plans made with fm.Workload(reproducible=True), which the planner refuses where it cannot guarantee it. Restart points rebuild the neighbour list, so for bitwise agreement set restart_every=None too.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text: fastmace run run.toml writes the same files. To quench frames of a finished run, see Relaxations and quenches.

docs.title: Prebuilt OEq host-extension wheels: fastmace-oeq-ext (plan task 6-T04)
docs.text: Owner decisions (plans/phase-6.md): D3 (a) torch 2.14.1+cu130 only; D4 (a) prebuilt wheels on PyPI as a separate package fastmace-oeq-ext, Linux x86_64, CPython 3.10 to 3.13.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
OpenEquivariance 0.7.0 builds a small C++ host extension (libtorch_tp_jit.so, pybind11 plus TORCH_LIBRARY ops) with torch.utils.cpp_extension.load at its first import, which needs g++ and ninja (oeq-runtime.md). Its device kernels are compiled with NVRTC at run time, so the host library is the only compiled part. fastmace-oeq-ext ships that library, built from OEq's unmodified sources against torch 2.14.1+cu130, one wheel per CPython:

Wheel Tag Contents fastmace_oeq_ext-0.7.0.post1-cp310-cp310-manylinux_2_28_x86_64.whl cp310 fastmace_oeq_ext/{__init__.py, libtorch_tp_jit.so, manifest.json, LICENSE.openequivariance, BUILD_COMPILER.txt} ...-cp311-cp311-... / ...-cp312-cp312-... cp311 / cp312 the same ...-cp313-cp313-... cp313 the same; Python 3.13 support added by 6-T15

dependencies = ["torch==2.14.1", "openequivariance==0.7.0"]. Licence MIT AND BSD-3-Clause: the packaging is FastMACE's MIT, the library OEq's BSD-3 (its licence ships in the wheel, as BSD-3 clause 2 requires for binaries). The version 0.7.0.postN follows OEq's; N counts rebuilds.

The library links libc10/libtorch*/libtorch_python (found through $ORIGIN/../torch/lib) and libcudart/libnvrtc/libcublas.so.13 ($ORIGIN/../nvidia/cu13/lib, the wheels torch already loads), and libcuda.so.1 from the driver. It does not link libpython (OEq's JIT build does, for its AOTI path only).

docs.title: How FastMACE picks it
docs.text:
fastmace.kernels._oeq_runtime.prebuilt_extension() reads fastmace_oeq_ext/manifest.json without importing anything and accepts it only if torch (with its +cu130 tag), OpenEquivariance and the CPython tag match exactly, the platform is Linux x86_64 and the library exists. Then prepare_in_process sets up the stand-in CUDA home as before (links only), and wraps torch.utils.cpp_extension.load so that OEq's load_jit_extension("libtorch_tp_jit", ...) gets the prebuilt module; nothing is compiled and no build cache is written. Otherwise it builds with the host toolchain, as before, and records why the wheel was not used (extension["prebuilt_skipped"]).

  • FASTMACE_OEQ_PREBUILT=0: never use the wheel. =1: refuse to build (the clean-install check uses it).
  • fastmace doctor prints host extension: prebuilt (fastmace-oeq-ext 0.7.0.post1, <path>); no compiler needed, or built with the host toolchain ...; prebuilt not used: <reason>, and only then requires g++ and ninja.
  • The run's patch record oeq_runtime (provenance, metadata.json) ends with host extension: prebuilt (<path>) or host extension: built|reused|raced|in-process.

pip install "fastmace[oeq]" pulls fastmace-oeq-ext with the marker sys_platform == 'linux' and platform_machine == 'x86_64' and python_version < '3.14'. On another torch pip refuses to resolve (torch==2.14.1 pin); install openequivariance alone to use the toolchain build.

docs.title: MACE PR draft: block and grouped linear for cuEquivariance Linear
docs.text: Upstream: ACEsuit/mace, base main at e37c8583a8b1b586e5888fa6dca86e8f591e2606 (merge of develop, 19 October 2026). Patch: 0001-block-linear.patch (new files only: mace/modules/block_linear.py, tests/unit/test_block_linear.py). Not opened (owner opens it, decision D5 (b)).

docs.title: Title
docs.text: Add an inference-time block-linear conversion for cuEquivariance Linear layers (per-l GEMMs, 2–12 % faster MD steps)

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text:
With enable_cueq=True, every equivariant linear layer of MACE is a cuet.Linear(method="naive") (mace/modules/wrapper_ops.py, Linear.__new__). For inference the weights are constant, and such a layer is block-diagonal: each input segment mul_in x ir maps to each output segment of the same irrep through one [mul_in, mul_out] matrix, applied alike to all 2l + 1 components. It can therefore run as one plain GEMM per (input segment, output segment) on [n * (2l + 1), mul] rows of the ir_mul layout.

This PR adds mace.modules.block_linear.convert_block_linears(model, grouped=True), an opt-in, inference-only conversion that:

  1. extracts each layer's effective weights from the module itself (linear.f on a unit basis), so path normalisation and layout are cuEquivariance's own and not re-derived;
  2. multiplies the input gradient (forces) by a precomputed contiguous transposed weight. The autograd backward otherwise multiplies by a transposed view, and cuBLAS picks slower kernels for it (15–25 % slower on MACE-MH-1's 512 x 512 blocks);
  3. with grouped=True (default) concatenates the same-irrep input segments that feed one output segment (the linear after the convolution: several 128x1o paths into one block) and multiplies them by their stacked weights in one GEMM, instead of one GEMM per path plus additions of wide outputs.

Nothing changes for training or for users who do not call the conversion.

docs.title: Measured gains (from our validation reports; same algorithm, FastMACE/research-engine implementation)
docs.text:
All MD-step timings are float32, cuEquivariance/OpenEquivariance hybrid, CUDA graphs, MACE-MH-1, 3x3x3 supercells, same-process A/B.

Change NaCl (216 atoms) NaNbO3 NbCl5 GPU Source block linear alone (per-l GEMMs + contiguous transposed backward) −11.8 % −1.5 % −0.9 % RTX 5060 Ti ResearchModule Experiments/Langevin_Thermostat/docs/roadmap.md item 12, 14 October 2026 grouped + merged residual (on top) −3.5 to −4.6 % −2.3 to −2.9 % −4.2 % RTX 4000 Ada (murphy) same, item 12, 16 October 2026; studies/other_models/README.md

Both passed the force-gate check (float32 force error against float64 at most 2x that of the stock float32 calculator) and the CUDA-graph replay gate. FastMACE carries them as registry records block_linear, grouped_linear (fastmace/rewrites/linear/), default on; see docs/rewrites.md.

The merged residual (one product per output segment over linear_1(message) and linear_res(linear_up(x)) of the MH-1-class RealAgnosticResidualNonLinearInteractionBlock) is not in this patch: it needs the interaction forward to divide by the density before linear_1, which is a separate change. It could follow as a second PR.

docs.title: Exactness
docs.text: Same terms, different summation order: exact up to floating-point rounding. In float64 the test agrees with cuet.Linear to 1e-12 (values and input gradients). Deterministic (no atomics).

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• inference only: weights are frozen buffers, gradients with respect to them are not computed;
  • not TorchScript/LAMMPS-exportable (custom autograd function); convert after export;
  • only cuet.Linear with internal shared weights and one weight class; others are left unchanged.

docs.title: Test plan
docs.text:
• [x] tests/unit/test_block_linear.py: float64, mul_ir and ir_mul, grouped and ungrouped, three irreps patterns (MH-1-like 128→512, repeated input irrep, output irrep without input) against cuet.Linear, values and input gradients; non-cuEq modules untouched. Run: 13 passed on MACE 0.3.16 / cuEquivariance 0.13.0 / torch 2.14.1+cpu (not on MACE main, which needs Python ≥ 3.11).
  • [ ] maintainers' CI on main (Python 3.11–3.14).
  • [ ] GPU: energy/forces of a converted mace-mp-0 medium vs unconverted, float32 and float64, and an MD-step timing (tests/benchmarks), to reproduce the table above with this plain-PyTorch version.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Gain depends on shapes and GPU. The 11.8 % on NaCl is small-system; large cells gain ~1 %. Expect smaller gains without CUDA graphs (launch overhead dominates small systems).
  • Weight extraction relies on linear.f([weight, x]) being cuEquivariance's polynomial call. If cuEquivariance changes that internal API, the conversion fails loudly (no silent wrong values), and the unit test catches it.
  • Memory: one extra transposed copy of every weight (a few MB for MH-1).
  • Users may forget the model is frozen; the docstring and the function name say so.

docs.title: MACE PR draft: reassociated first interaction
docs.text: Upstream: ACEsuit/mace, base main at e37c8583a8b1b586e5888fa6dca86e8f591e2606 (19 October 2026). Patch: 0001-reassociate-first.patch (new files only: mace/modules/reassociate.py, tests/unit/test_reassociate.py). Not opened (owner opens it, decision D5 (b)).

docs.title: Title
docs.text: Add an inference-time reassociation of the first interaction: sum edges per (receiver, sender species) before the radial projection

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text:
In the first interaction block the sender features are species-only scalars (linear_up(node_embedding(one_hot))), and the convolution is channelwise with one radial weight per (path, channel). Today every edge forms its [P*C] tensor-product weights (conv_tp_weights, e.g. 4 x 128 = 512 values per edge) and the tensor product, then sums per receiver. Because the last radial layer is affine and the sender features depend only on the sender's species, the sums can be reassociated:

m[i, l, m, u] = gamma_l  sum_z x[z, u]  sum_k W[path(l)·C + u, k]  S[i, z, k, (l, m)]
S[i, z, k, (l, m)] = sum_{edges j→i, species(j)=z}  a[e, k] Y[e, (l, m)],     a[e] = [h_e c_e, c_e]

S is a small edge sum over K ≈ 65 hidden radial features (plus a bias column), and the projection is one dense GEMM per path over [atoms·(2l+1), species·K]. The per-edge weights are never formed.

The conversion reassociate_first_interaction(model, species_columns=None) needs no change to any interaction forward: it swaps conv_tp_weights for "hidden layers, then append a 1 column" (the forward's existing * cutoff produces a), and conv_tp for a module with the fused calling convention (conv_fusion), which gets node_attrs from a forward pre-hook. gamma_l and the output layout are measured from the model's own conv_tp (e3nn, cuEquivariance or OpenEquivariance), so no normalisation convention is assumed. The conversion returns False and leaves the model unchanged where the form does not hold (non-scalar sender irreps, non-channelwise TP, non-affine last radial layer, models with joint_embedding).

docs.title: Measured gains (FastMACE / research-engine implementation of the same algorithm)
docs.text:
Model Change NaCl NaNbO3 NbCl5 GPU Source MACE-MH-1 plain PyTorch prototype (as in this patch) −0.6 to −2.6 % RTX 5060 Ti ResearchModule docs/roadmap.md item 11.2, 10 October 2026 MACE-MH-1 with a fused Triton backward of the edge sum −4.9 % −7.2 % −4.9 % RTX 5060 Ti same MP-0, MPA-0, OMAT-0, MatPES and other non-MH-1 benchmark models with the receiver-streaming convolution, together −16 to −28 % RTX 5060 Ti docs/roadmap.md item 13, studies/other_models/README.md, 15 October 2026 MACE-OMOL-0 reassociation added −9 % RTX 5060 Ti AGENTS.md / studies/other_models/README.md, 16 October 2026

MD-step times, float32 hybrid, CUDA graphs, 3x3x3 cells. All passed the force and graph-replay gates. FastMACE: records reassociate_first (MH-1 family, fastmace/rewrites/mh1/) and generic_reassociate (fastmace/rewrites/generic/); float64 agreement 1.3e-16 to 3.2e-15 eV/Å on mp0-medium (docs/validation/1a-T08-generic-rewrites.md). Its edge-sum cost after the rewrite is 0.06 ms (NaCl) to 0.5 ms (NbCl5) per force call (docs/validation/2-T20a-step-breakdown.md).

Honest expectation for this patch: it is the plain PyTorch form (an index_add_ of outer products, autograd backward). Our measurements say most of the gain needs a fused backward of the edge sum; this PR is the correct, general base on which such a kernel can be added later.

docs.title: Exactness
docs.text: The same products in a different summation order: exact up to rounding. The float64 test agrees with the unconverted model to 1e-10 eV (energy) and 1e-9 eV/Å (forces) on Residual, DensityResidual and ResidualNonLinear first blocks. index_add_ on CUDA uses atomics: not bitwise reproducible on GPU (as MACE's scatter_sum already is).

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• inference only (weights frozen into a buffer);
  • memory of S is atoms x species x (lmax+1)^2 x (K+1); pass species_columns (the elements a simulation can contain) for 89-element foundation models;
  • the converted model is not TorchScript-exportable (forward pre-hook with kwargs, Python state);
  • the species table x is read back from node_feats with index_reduce_(amax), which assumes that every atom of a species has identical first-layer features (true for species-only embeddings; models with joint_embedding are refused).

docs.title: Test plan
docs.text:
• [x] tests/unit/test_reassociate.py: float64 three-species MACE models with each residual first block, energy and forces against the unconverted model, with and without species_columns. Run: 6 passed on MACE 0.3.16 / torch 2.14.1+cpu (MACE main itself not run: Python 3.10 environment).
  • [ ] maintainers' CI on main.
  • [ ] GPU: mace-mp-0 medium and MH-1 with enable_cueq and enable_oeq (the conv_fusion probe path), float32 force check, MD-step timing.
  • [ ] a model whose conv_tp_weights is e3nn's FullyConnectedNet with normalised weights (affinity probe covers it; add an explicit test).

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Small or no gain without a fused backward, as measured (0.6–2.6 %). Reviewers may prefer to wait for a kernel.
  • Probing relies on internal structure (interaction.edge_irreps, edge_attrs_irreps, conv_tp.weight_numel, radial net layer list). Any mismatch returns False rather than producing wrong numbers, and the affinity of the last radial layer is checked numerically.
  • Pre-hook state (conv_tp.node_attrs) is per call; concurrent calls of one model object from two threads would race (MACE does not do this).

docs.title: OpenEquivariance PR draft: build the JIT host extension from the NVIDIA runtime wheels (no toolkit, no nvcc)
docs.text: Upstream: PASSIONLab/OpenEquivariance, base main at dc9979099c65113adcc016977c5c60974f9ddafb (27 September 2026, after v0.7.0). Patch: 0001-wheel-cuda-host-build.patch: edits openequivariance/openequivariance/_torch/extlib/__init__.py, adds .../extlib/wheel_cuda.py and tests/wheel_cuda_test.py. Not opened (owner opens it, decision D5 (b)).

docs.title: Title
docs.text: JIT extension: build against the pip NVIDIA CUDA wheels when no CUDA toolkit is installed

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text:
The torch host extension libtorch_tp_jit has only C++ sources; its device kernels are compiled at run time with NVRTC. Building it needs the CUDA runtime headers and link libraries, not nvcc. A PyTorch install from PyPI already ships both in the NVIDIA wheels (nvidia/cu13/{include,lib} for CUDA 13; nvidia/cuda_runtime, cuda_nvrtc, cublas, cuda_cccl for CUDA 12). But load_jit_extension() calls include_paths("cuda") and library_paths("cuda"), which require torch.utils.cpp_extension.CUDA_HOME. On machines without a toolkit (shared HPC workstations, cloud images, Colab-like VMs, containers built from python: images) CUDA_HOME is None, the build fails, and MACE silently runs without OEq. Where the precompiled extension does not apply (torch < 2.10, OEQ_JIT_EXTENSION=1, HIP), users currently need a toolkit or a wrapper script that fakes one.

We ran OEq 0.7 on toolkit-less workstations for weeks through such a wrapper (a directory of symbolic links standing in for CUDA_HOME, plus an nvcc sentinel that fails loudly), later replaced by in-process preparation in FastMACE (fastmace/kernels/_oeq_runtime.py; findings in docs/design/oeq-runtime.md). The sentinel was never invoked: no step of the build needs nvcc. This PR removes the need for any such wrapper.

docs.title: Change
docs.text:
• new extlib/wheel_cuda.py: wheel_build_flags() finds the wheel directories in site-packages and returns explicit include directories (with CCCL) and linker arguments that link each library by soname (-l:libcudart.so.13, -l:libnvrtc.so.13, -l:libcublas.so.13, driver -l:libcuda.so.1) with an RPATH to the wheel. No CUDA_HOME and no unversioned lib*.so links are needed. The driver directory is searched in the usual places (/usr/lib/wsl/lib, multiarch, /usr/lib64, /usr/lib64-nvidia) or taken from OEQ_CUDA_DRIVER_DIR.
  • load_jit_extension() (CUDA branch only): new variable OEQ_CUDA_FROM_WHEELS = auto (default: wheels only when CUDA_HOME is None, so existing toolkit builds are unchanged), 1 (always; error if the wheels are missing), 0 (never). With the wheels, the device include path is include_paths("cpu") plus the wheel's.
  • HIP and SYCL branches untouched.

docs.title: Why linking by soname matters
docs.text: On one of our workstations the libpython directory (/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu) also holds a system CUDA 11.5's development links (libnvrtc.so, libcudart.so). OEq passes -L<libpython dir> before the CUDA directories, so -lnvrtc resolved to CUDA 11 and the extension mixed runtimes. -l:libnvrtc.so.13 plus -L<wheel> cannot pick a different major version.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
• Local PC, WSL2, RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130, OEq 0.7.0, nvidia-cuda-runtime 13.0.96, g++ 13.3: check_wheel_build.py (in this folder) builds OEq 0.7.0's host sources with only the new flags, CUDA_HOME/CUDA_PATH unset, no nvcc on PATH: built in 18–20 s, loaded with torch.ops.load_library, and ldd shows libcudart.so.13, libnvrtc.so.13, libcublas.so.13 (and libcublasLt.so.13) from nvidia/cu13/lib and libcuda.so.1 from the driver.
  • The equivalent symbolic-link layout (same headers, same libraries) has built and run OEq 0.7.0 with MACE on four workstations (RTX A4000, RTX 4000 Ada x2, RTX 5060 Ti) since 8 October 2026; forces of the in-process route agree with the wrapper-script route to 3.9e-7 eV/Å, the same scatter as two runs of the script itself (docs/design/oeq-runtime.md, run table).

docs.title: Exactness
docs.text: Build-system change only; the compiled code is the same. No effect on kernels.

docs.title: Test plan
docs.text:
• [x] tests/wheel_cuda_test.py (CPU, no GPU): cu13 layout found and flags correct (CCCL include, sonames, one -L per directory, driver last); missing wheel and missing library return None. Run: 3 passed, 1 skipped (in torch 2.14.1+cu130, Python 3.10).
  • [x] build check on a toolkit-less configuration (above), with OEq 0.7.0 sources and the flags this patch computes.
  • [ ] OEQ_TEST_WHEEL_BUILD=1 pytest tests/wheel_cuda_test.py on a GPU host with the patched package (imports openequivariance._torch.extlib in a subprocess without CUDA_HOME). Not run: we did not install the patched upstream main.
  • [ ] verify_extension_build.yml: add a job leg on a runner image without the CUDA toolkit.
  • [ ] CUDA 12 wheels (torch==2.x+cu126): untested; the code path exists.
  • [ ] then tests/conv_test.py / batch_test.py with the wheel-built extension.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• auto changes behaviour only where the build failed before (CUDA_HOME is None); with a toolkit the old path runs. Users with a toolkit and wheels keep the toolkit (set =1 to prefer the wheels).
  • Header/runtime skew: the wheel's headers match the wheel's libraries by construction, which is safer than a system toolkit of another version, but a torch built for CUDA 12 next to a stray cu13 wheel would pick cu13 first (layout order). Could be refined by preferring the major version of torch.version.cuda.
  • -l: syntax is GNU ld / lld / gold; not macOS (not a CUDA target) or MSVC (Windows is not supported by the JIT path today).
  • Driver lookup heuristics may miss unusual installs; OEQ_CUDA_DRIVER_DIR overrides.
  • Interaction with the existing stale-lock wait (_wait_for_torch_build_lock): unchanged.
